PullRequest.Title: ci: cache Playwright browsers for pull request browser tests
PullRequest.Body:
Caches Playwright's browsers for the GitHub browser-test jobs, so a CDN incident no longer fails them. This is the GitHub half of B11. An ADO PR follows once #343325 lands.

## Why

Over the last 14 days, out of 15,508 GitHub workflow runs, 4 jobs failed only in a Playwright browser-download step. That's 2 in `component-fixtures` today with `ERR_TLS_CERT_ALTNAME_INVALID` from `cdn.playwright.dev`, 1 in `monaco-editor` today, and 1 in `pr.yml` (macOS) on Oct 13. The existing 3-attempt retry loops can't outlast a CDN problem that lasts minutes.

## What

- **New `.github/actions/restore-playwright`, modeled on `restore-wsl-installer`.**
  - It sets `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` to `.build/ms-playwright` for the rest of the job.
  - It restores that directory from a cache keyed on `runner.os`, `runner.arch`, the pinned `playwright` version from `package-lock.json`, and the install arguments.
  - With `save-cache: 'true'`, it downloads the browsers with `npx playwright@<version> install …` on a miss and saves them, the same way the other warm-on-main caches work.
- **`pr-{linux,darwin,win32}-test.yml`** restore it right before the existing install step, which is unchanged. On a hit, `playwright install` finds the browsers and downloads nothing. On a miss, it downloads exactly as today, retry loop included.
- **`pr-node-modules.yml`** warms the cache on main in the Linux, macOS and Windows jobs. The step is `continue-on-error`, like the WSL one. `detect-missing-caches` computes these keys, and `detectMissingCaches.test.ts` checks that the jobs, keys, versions and the action stay in sync.
- **`component-fixtures.yml`** restores in both jobs. It saves on pushes to main, where that workflow already runs. The fixture-tests job uses its own `test/componentFixtures/playwright/package-lock.json`.
- **`monaco-editor.yml` is left out.** It runs only on pull requests and installs every browser, and it had one hit in 14 days.

## Validation

- `node --test build/lib/test/detectMissingCaches.test.ts` passes 4/4 with the new cache.
- I ran the action's prepare script locally against both lockfiles. It resolves `1.61.1` and sets keys such as `playwright-v1-macOS-ARM64-1.61.1-only-shell-chromium-webkit`.
- All touched YAML parses, eslint is clean, and `tsc -p build` reports nothing in the touched files.
- **Cold and warm, on this PR:** a temporary commit makes the Linux job save the cache, so one run populates it (cold) and the next restores it (warm). That commit will be dropped before review. Evidence will be posted here.

> Authored with Copilot

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The job gates, normal restore behavior, lack of downstream browser use, and existing lookup-only repository pattern are all explicit in the changed workflows. Archive size and exact duration vary by browser version, but the unnecessary network/extraction mechanism and critical-path placement do not.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Playwright browser cache archive bytes, filesystem writes, and decompression CPU
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The wasted restore occurs once for each Linux, macOS, or Windows warming job that runs because any other cache for that platform is missing; its cost scales with the cached browser set, especially the macOS Chromium plus WebKit archive.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased cache-warming job latency, network I/O, disk I/O, and runner CPU
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR, these platform warming jobs did not fetch or extract Playwright browser archives. Existing warm-only resources such as the WSL installer explicitly use actions/cache lookup-only mode.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Each new Cache Playwright browsers step invokes restore-playwright with save-cache true, but the composite action always performs a normal actions/cache/restore. Therefore an exact browser-cache hit downloads and extracts the archive even though pr-node-modules never runs browser tests or otherwise consumes the restored files.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added pr-node-modules.yml lines 207-213 (and analogous macOS/Windows additions) place restore-playwright in warm-only jobs; added restore-playwright/action.yml lines 37-43 perform a full cache restore on every hit rather than a metadata lookup.
Findings.Title: Use lookup-only mode in the cache-warming jobs
Findings.Impact: After an unrelated node_modules, Electron, WSL, or detector miss starts a platform job while the Playwright cache is already warm, that job unnecessarily downloads and extracts a large browser archive before it can finish. This adds substantial CI latency and bandwidth on up to three platform jobs per dependency/cache change.
Findings.Evidence: The platform gates run when any cache in getCaches is missing, not specifically Playwright (.github/actions/detect-missing-caches/detect.ts:160-170 and pr-node-modules.yml:121/217/302). The added steps at lines 207, 292, and 384 all set save-cache true. restore-playwright/action.yml:37-43 uses actions/cache/restore without lookup-only, while the analogous warm-only restore-wsl-installer/action.yml:23 passes lookup-only when save-cache is true. No later step in any of these three jobs uses .build/ms-playwright.
Findings.Recommendation: Add an explicit lookup-only input to restore-playwright and set it to true in the three pr-node-modules warming calls, while leaving it false for browser-test/component-fixture consumers that need the files. On a miss, continue downloading and saving exactly as today.

Scenarios.Scenario: Pull-request browser tests on Linux, macOS, and Windows
Scenarios.CriticalPath: For jobs with BROWSER_TESTS=true, the new cache restore must finish before the existing playwright install and all browser tests. On an exact hit it replaces the browser CDN download; on a miss the existing install remains the browser-download critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Download and extract the Playwright browser archive through actions/cache/restore.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One exact-key restore attempt per browser-test job; one archive transfer on a warm hit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The job proceeded directly to playwright install and downloaded the same browser set from the Playwright CDN.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before browser installation and test execution.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Install the selected Playwright browsers through the existing npm exec playwright install retry loop.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical install per participating platform job, up to three attempts on failure; on a cache hit it validates local files and downloads no browser.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Always downloaded the selected browsers when they were absent; this remains the cold-miss behavior.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One browser archive per participating OS/architecture job: Chromium headless shell on Linux and Windows, Chromium headless shell plus WebKit on macOS. Browser arguments and the pinned Playwright version determine effective archive cardinality.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each workflow job performs one restore; platform jobs can run independently in parallel, while work inside each job is serialized before its browser tests. The existing install retains a three-attempt retry loop.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Exact cache keys include runner OS, runner architecture, pinned Playwright version, and normalized install arguments, with no prefix fallback. Warm hits restore the archive; cold misses fall through to the unchanged install, and main-branch warming supplies future hits. Failures are not negatively cached.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the environment path, exact key, restore placement, and unchanged downstream install are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact cache compression ratio, transfer duration, and hit rate depend on GitHub cache service and browser release size.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression on this consumer path: warm runs substitute a cache transfer for a CDN browser download, while cold behavior preserves one browser download.

Scenarios.Scenario: Main-branch cache warming and missing-cache detection
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The detector lists every expected cache before platform jobs can be skipped or launched. If any cache for a platform is absent or detection fails, that platform job runs; all of its steps, including the new Playwright step, must finish before the job completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List cache versions through the GitHub Actions cache REST API.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional API request for each of Linux, macOS, and Windows; requests within each platform are parallel with its other cache lookups.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No Playwright cache lookup was made; existing cache families were queried.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Detection must finish before all warming job gates resolve.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Restore and extract an exact-hit Playwright browser archive in each launched warming job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to one archive transfer per launched platform job, including when only an unrelated cache caused the job to run.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Warming jobs did not fetch Playwright browser files; analogous WSL warming uses lookup-only to avoid restoring hit contents.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The unused transfer and extraction delay completion of each launched platform job.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: On a Playwright miss, download browsers from the Playwright CDN and upload the resulting archive to GitHub cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One browser install and one save per missing platform key, with install retried up to three times.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These warming jobs performed no Playwright browser download or cache upload.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required to populate a genuinely missing browser cache; continue-on-error prevents failure from blocking job success but the step duration remains on the job path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Three new Playwright cache keys/API lookups, then at most one browser archive per launched Linux, macOS, or Windows job. A platform job may be launched by a node_modules, Electron, WSL, or Playwright miss.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Cache-version requests for one platform are Promise.all-coalesced, but platforms are checked sequentially. Linux, macOS, and Windows warming jobs can run concurrently; workflow concurrency allows one active and one pending main run. Browser work is one operation per platform, not per package.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The detector distinguishes exact key/version hits and launches a platform job on any miss. On a Playwright miss the action downloads and saves the browser set. On a hit, the action currently performs a full restore even though these warming jobs do not consume the files; there is no lookup-only mode on these calls.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the any-cache job gate, full restore action, and absence of downstream browser use are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser archive byte sizes, unrelated-cache miss frequency, and cache eviction frequency determine aggregate wasted transfer time.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable regression: exact-hit browser archives are eagerly restored in warm-only jobs launched for unrelated misses. An explicit lookup-only input preserves warming semantics without the transfer.

Scenarios.Scenario: Component fixture tests and screenshot rendering on pull requests and branch pushes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each of the two parallel jobs restores the browser cache before its existing playwright install and test/render step. On pushes, a miss also downloads and saves the browser before the consumer runs.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Restore the shared Chromium cache in each component-fixture job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two restore attempts per workflow run and, on warm runs, two isolated archive downloads—one per runner.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Each job downloaded Chromium through its existing playwright install.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each restore precedes and gates that job's install and browser workload.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: On a cold branch push, install Chromium and save the resulting GitHub cache archive.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Potentially once in each of the two concurrent jobs for the same cold key, followed by competing saves; this matches the prior two Chromium downloads and adds cache upload work only on the cold population run.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Both jobs independently downloaded Chromium and did not upload a shared cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The download remains required before tests/rendering; cache save is serialized before the following existing install.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the selected package-lock and write PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH/job outputs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per job over one lockfile; bounded small synchronous reads/writes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Two Ubuntu jobs, each requesting Chromium 1.61.1 under the current lockfiles. Because OS, architecture, version, and browser arguments match, both currently address the same cache key.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The Playwright fixture and screenshot jobs run concurrently and may race on a cold push. Each performs one restore/install sequence. Existing workflow-level cancellation coalesces superseded runs by PR number or SHA.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Pull requests restore only; main/release pushes restore and save on misses. Warm runs transfer the shared Chromium archive into each isolated runner. On a simultaneous cold push both jobs may miss and download, but both already downloaded Chromium independently before the PR, so browser-download cardinality is not increased; one cache save may win the identical key.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both job inputs, lockfile versions, concurrency, and downstream consumers are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact benefit depends on cache hit rate and relative GitHub-cache versus Playwright-CDN throughput; cold concurrent save conflict behavior is service-dependent.
Scenarios.Verdict: No actionable performance regression: warm restores replace two prior browser downloads, and cold browser-download multiplicity remains two while enabling later reuse.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all nine changed files and traced PR browser tests, main cache warming/detection, and component-fixture consumers. Submitted one medium eager-I/O finding for full browser archive restores in warm-only platform jobs; no other changed mechanism met the regression threshold.
